\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
\noindent This course teaches the simulation of \emph{morphology} in
organic-electronic thin films --- the coupled phase separation and
crystallization of polymer/small-molecule/solvent blends that decides
how organic solar cells, transistors, and bioelectronic devices
perform. It is built around \textbf{OrgElMorph}, a GPU-native,
differentiable phase-field simulator. Three tracks run in parallel:
the \emph{physics} of the models, the \emph{computation} that makes
them fast and correct, and the \emph{differentiation} that turns the
simulator into an instrument for design and inference. Every concept
pairs a written explanation with a runnable tutorial; you reproduce the
figures and numbers here, then explore the questions on your own.
\end{abstract}

\tableofcontents

\chapter{Using this course}
Read a concept below, then open its tutorial folder
(\file{tutorials/orgelmorph-course/<track>/<NN\_name>/}), run
\file{run.py}, and compare your printed self-check table and figures
with the ones in this document. The tutorials call the same production
solver the research code uses. The three tracks cross-reference each
other; a first pass straight down the Physics track is a good start,
dipping into the matching Computational and Differentiable concepts as
they are referenced.

Boxes flag the two things you act on:
\begin{keybox}\textbf{Key idea.} The load-bearing concept.\end{keybox}
\begin{runbox}\textbf{Run it.} The command, and what to compare.\end{runbox}
Questions marked \textbf{\textcolor{purple!70!black}{Q}} are for you to
explore --- they have no answers printed here on purpose.
